title: OpsForge lab toolchain documents (contract 1)
description: The documents of `opsforge api`: inputs (stdin, or HTTP request bodies) and outputs (stdout, or HTTP responses; contract/openapi.yaml) of run|probe|heal|validate-steps|version and sandbox, and the HTTP API's sandboxes, jobs, problems and file listings (contract/README.md). Steps are scenario steps (lab/scenario.py); their placeholders are resolved by the toolchain, `${ns}` with the sandbox's namespace. Inputs are strict. Outputs may gain fields in a minor version: readers ignore the ones they do not know (OpsForge's golden documents pin exactly what it prints).

log.description: Human-readable lines, each starting with the seconds since the run began.

error.description: Why the run stopped early (a failing step, a missing node); null when every step ran.

requires.description: What the sandbox needs from the running lab (a course's requirements). OpsForge checks them before creating it: 409 /problems/unmet-requirements names what is missing.

needs.description: vpn: interconnect vpn; k3s: a K3s cluster; monitoring, ci: those nodes

faults.description: setup breaks links (partition, degrade, ...): deleting the sandbox heals the lab, and no other sandbox may exist meanwhile

cluster_changes.description: setup changes the cluster outside the sandbox's namespace (teardown undoes it): no other sandbox may exist meanwhile

sandboxInput.description: POST /v1/sandboxes: one lab or challenge attempt. Created as a job: the workspace with `files`, the namespace (namespace: true), then `setup`; a failing setup is cleaned up at once (teardown, namespace, heal) and the sandbox is `failed`. Deleting it runs `teardown`, deletes the namespace, heals when `requires.faults` and deletes the workspace.

label.description: What it is for, shown to the lab's owner (e.g. lab nodes-and-regions, attempt 7)

namespace.description: true: a namespace sb-<id> on every K3s cluster (needs k3s), ${ns} in steps, the default namespace of `opsforge kubectl` in the sandbox

files.description: The workspace's first files: relative path -> UTF-8 content (the workspace limits apply)

expires_after.description: Seconds without a call after which OpsForge deletes the sandbox (default 86400)

sandboxOutput.description: A sandbox. Steps run on the lab host in its workspace, with `opsforge` on the PATH and its namespace as `opsforge kubectl`'s default.

status.description: creating, then ready or failed (setup failed: already cleaned up); resetting; deleting; deleted (only in the delete job's output)

placeholders.description: The lab's placeholders (state's) plus ${ns}: for the client's texts

setup.description: The last setup's runOutput, null before it ends

teardown.description: The teardown's runOutput (after a failed setup, or in the delete job's output), else null

expires_at.description: When OpsForge deletes it unless a call comes first

actionInput.description: POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/actions: steps run in the sandbox (a challenge's test action); fault steps refused. Output: runOutput.

runInput.description: `opsforge api run` (the CLI only, for authors): a phase's steps, outside any sandbox.

probeInput.description: A probe check: steps that only observe the lab (fault steps refused in a sandbox) and what passing means. `opsforge api probe`, or POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/probes.

results.description: One per expectation, in `expect` order. checked is false for a step the probe never reached (it stops at the first failing named step).

healed.description: false when there was no fault to heal

sets.description: Sets of scenario steps to check without running them: a lab's setup or teardown, a check's probe (with its expect).

faults.description: false: fault steps (partition, degrade, ...) are refused, as in a check that only observes the lab

errors.description: Why steps would not run, in set order; empty when every set is valid.

set.description: Index of the set in the input

problem.description: Why a call failed (RFC 9457 fields): on stderr from the CLI, as the body of an HTTP error (application/problem+json), or a failed job's `problem`.

unmet.description: With /problems/unmet-requirements: what the running lab lacks, one entry each

jobOutput.description: Lab work started over HTTP (a sandbox's create, reset, probe, action or delete, or heal): `log` grows while it runs; once done, `output` is its output document (sandboxOutput for create, reset and delete, probeOutput for probe, runOutput for action, healOutput for heal); failed: `problem` says why (not a failing step: that is the output's `error`). One lab job at a time.

sandbox.description: The sandbox it works on (known from the 202 on), null for heal

output.description: The output document once done, else null

filesOutput.description: A sandbox's workspace: its regular files (GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/files), by path, and their total size.

minor.description: Additive revisions of this major: a caller gates what it sends on it
